freeze.pilot: The frozen README records 1 closure among 150 starts with seed 11, with both laws agreeing on outcomes. The full run reads all 7,075 starts and so includes the pilot population. There is no separate local pilot archive or saved roster.

predictions.K1: At most 2%. The archived 171/7,075 is 2.417%, so it fails by 30 closures above the greatest allowed integer count of 141. The decision reports this failure without moving the threshold.
predictions.K2: The bounded size prediction holds in the archive, with a maximum of nine displayed rules. Its rationale for K3 was outside the earlier census's hypotheses. Of the 171 newly closed stages, 169 have at least one rule with more than three places. The earlier negative covers 27 connected three-place classes with at most one shared distinction between any two knots. The general claim that closure is necessary had already been refuted.
predictions.K3: Both strict box counts are zero. The birth-essential part follows from that zero and had zero possible source-law deletion tests.

freeze.implementation_bounds: closed.py:16–18 and 33–41 specify the default full search at up to 20 distinctions and a cap of 50 boxes per stage for source-law deletion tests. The archive reaches 15 distinctions with no search omissions and no box on which the deletion cap could matter. At closed.py:26–32 a successful sixth round is counted immediately, without testing whether the resulting stage has a loose distinction. A replay must check the round-six boundary directly.
freeze.post_hoc: There is no post/ within this study folder. The related strict open witness is the predecessor replay in research/UPPER-GROWN-20261127-001/post/grown_replay.json, with its script beside it. It reproduces the exact ordinary grown stage, 14,554 allowed states, seven upper words and all twelve source laws essential. It tests a built ten-knot start under ordinary growth.

archive_cross_check_per_law.opportunity_note: The two numerical opportunity filters are necessary for the frozen strict box. They do not check the signs, disjointness or upper reading itself. Counts are per law, and different starts can reach an identical or relabelled stage.

prior_work.method: The objects subcommand dispatches directly to search_objects; it opens SQLite with mode=ro and only calls object_rows SELECTs. Epic and optional deep scans read files. The database header was 1/1 (rollback journal), with no journal sidecar present. Read-only queries used the repository Python, bytecode writes disabled, single-thread settings and a 1 GiB virtual-memory cap. The first three-row query took 0.26 s and about 41 MiB peak resident memory. The date filters epic IDs inclusively, so later corrections can appear in results dated the same day. Freeze order was checked against Git history.
prior_work.query_prefix: OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 BLAS=1 .venv/bin/python -B scripts/track.py objects

relevant_predecessors.finding: The strict upper form was already known on a chosen closed twelve-knot start. An overlap version already bound on the open three-knot ring after three and four ordinary rounds, with a round-three law needed.

Prior strict census: 49/85 simple closed twelve-knot classes under equal class weighting (368/661 under equal labelled weighting), 0/27 smaller classes, 0/2,416 sampled stages. The later referee found 18 strict boxes on a built ordinary open stage and one four-clause form on a closed ten-knot source and one on a sampled grown stage.

The 49 seeded cuts miss every strict box, one of the 882 cuts gives 18 strict boxes, and allowing overlap within each paired comparison gives an upper binding on all 49 seeded cuts. None of these populations is the rival-law census.
The two rival grants and their ability to close a chosen start under not-all-equal were known. The new frozen result is the closure census and strict box recount on that census.

A three-knot ring with one extra loose distinction at each of two knots fits this census. On it A129 retains 146 of 146 old states and A130 retains 106 of 146, so the rivalry differs before a stall. A five-knot start with repeated meetings also fits the census when it has the extra loose distinction z. After growth under both laws, an eight-place displayed rule loses K2 in the actual projection. Thus claims about the imposed rule count and the canonical knot count need distinct evidence.
The two rival cuts were already found to bind old ring parities under a chosen parity reading on a built start. That result uses different source laws and readings from the strict not-all-equal box.
Ordinary growth from open starts can close under parity but supplies a fresh distinction under not-all-equal. The law name and initial openness matter in the frozen introduction.

prior_work.search_limit: No earlier record returned the same 171-of-7,075 six-round not-all-equal closure census with the strict-box exclusion. The internal index and bounded matching file searches do not establish an external novelty claim. Other high-ranked results concern different populations or relations.

intuition.status: Exact link with an inexpensive diagnostic
intuition.statement: An unread private distinction supplies a local extension of every assignment to the rest of a knot's variables. If all six readings ignore such a variable of a source rule, every reading word after deleting that rule already occurred with it. This is the same extension mechanism behind ordinary growth's preserved projection. An essential birth can use a private distinction only if a carrier reads it. Closing is one way of removing these private extension choices.
intuition.cheapest_test: For a proposed birth-essential witness, delete one source rule at a time. If a new upper word appears, check whether the rule still held a private distinction and whether a carrier included it. The ordinary open witness provides the positive control because its carriers read both fresh distinctions.
